open.evidence: Checked at HEAD 5f266ca83 (worktree clean). Both claimed fixes are in the code. First, `_reconcile_active` now records active-orders evidence one order per transaction (engine.py:1851-1875). A refused row goes to `_evidence_refused` (1877-1888), which adds the cell to `evidence_conflicts` (a scoped TP block, 2154) and sets manual reconcile, so the engine goes FROZEN. Second, the tick-level StoreError/LedgerError handler (812-824) calls `_recover_after_refusal` (826-852). That reloads, re-evaluates, runs `_act` unless the phase was act/finish, and commits the snapshot. The round-3 tests test_d102_recurring_active_row_contradiction_is_isolated_and_frozen_is_committed and test_d204_any_recurring_store_refusal_still_commits_frozen_and_keeps_risk_reducing_work pass. The in-memory mutations in verify3/ngmut3.py make them fail: d102_iso (per-order catch removed) fails d102, and d204_norecover / d102_noact / d204_nocommit fail d204. The earlier probe verify/test_probe_d102.py (recurring initial_base_amount 11 != 10 on A) now passes: B TP LIVE, 9 outside-bounds cancels, FROZEN. The new probe verify3/test_probe_v2.py::test_d102_recurring_settle_refusal (close_cycle refused for cell A every tick) shows the other cell's TP placed, 16 cancels and a committed FROZEN snapshot. The original OVERFILL scenario still works after a restart (::test_d102_original_overfill_then_restart: B TP placed, 9 cancels). The verifier's residual (a recurring refusal in `_scan_history`) still reproduces after a restart. `startup_reconciled` is set only after a complete walk has been applied (1616-1622). RECONCILING is then added to tp_blockers (2038-2040), and `_act` sends risk-reducing cancels only when startup_reconciled (2435). ::test_d102_recurring_history_refusal_after_restart (a recurring history-apply StoreError after restart) gives tp_blockers ['RECONCILING'] and 0 outside-bounds cancels. ::test_cr2_restart_with_conflict (a persistent scanner-withheld payload conflict on cell 3, then a restart) shows another cell with committed E=10, no TP, tp_blockers ['RECONCILING'], 0 cancels and 9 entries left live. This is the finding's symptom: one cell's history conflict withholds every cell's exits and outside-bounds cancels until an operator acks.
open.residual_risk: After any restart, a single cell's persistent withheld history conflict, or a recurring history-apply refusal, keeps the walk incomplete indefinitely. Every cell's TP obligations and every OUTSIDE_BOUNDS/retry cancel are then withheld, while resting entries can keep filling, until an operator acks. This contradicts NG-OPS-001, NG-OPS-002 and NG-DB-003 step 6. No test pins the restart case. A further minor gap, stated by design ('unless the refusal came from acting'): a refusal that recurs inside `_act` is not recovered. An injected record_cancel_intent refusal on the lowest CID gave 0 of 8 outside-bounds cancels (::test_d102_recurring_act_refusal_cancel). This one is contrived, because the reload makes memory match the store.

open.evidence: `_withheld_conflict_cells` (engine.py:2161-2188) maps `scanner.last_conflicted_rows` to cells by own CID or exchange order id, and `_scoped_tp_blocks` (2156-2159) adds those cells. An unattributable row adds HISTORY_CONFLICT_UNATTRIBUTED to both the TP and entry blockers (2028-2030). The earlier probe verify/test_probe_ack_conflict.py::test_probe_tp_dispatched_for_cell_with_contradicted_fill now prints `tp_blocked_cells: {3: 'HISTORY_CONFLICT:withheld trades row'}`, `E: 5 TPs: []`. At the previous HEAD it printed TP 5 LIVE. The C2 tests pass. Mutation c2_all fails both of them, c2_scope fails the attributed test, and c2_unattr fails the unattributed test. Across a restart cell A stays blocked (RECONCILING, then the withheld mapping). The block is derived only from the in-memory scanner result of the last finished walk, though. history.py:841 replaces `last_conflicted_rows` on every finished walk, and nothing durable records the conflicted cell: the manual-reconcile evidence holds only the conflict strings. Probe verify3/test_probe_v2.py::test_cr2_transient_conflict_then_tp uses inject_conflicting_trade(persistent=False). One walk sees T1 as both 3 and 1 (duplicate_key_payload_mismatch), and the store sets manual reconcile 'history conflict', so the engine is FROZEN. The next walk sees only 3, so `tp_blocked_cells` becomes {} and history is complete. A further fill of 2 makes E=5, and a TP of 5 is dispatched LIVE while the engine is still FROZEN, manual_reconcile_required=True, and no ack was given.
open.residual_risk: A contradiction that the venue serves only once or intermittently unblocks the contradicted cell's TP after the next clean walk, although the conflict is still unaudited and the engine is FROZEN. The TP is then built from the committed quantity. If the contradicting value was the true one, the cell over-closes (by 2 LIT in the probe), which is the critic's failure mode on a narrower trigger. No test covers a non-persistent contradiction. A fix would record the conflicted cell durably, for example in engine_meta or the manual-reconcile evidence, until ack_history_conflict.

open.evidence: engine.py:1440-1463 `_absence_not_proven` now requires all of: settlement_delay_s since the dispatch; no `str(cid)` in ws_pending; an active list read after dispatch + delay and still fresh; `settlement_scans` complete walks that started after dispatch + delay. review3::test_d215 (active_lag 7) passes and fails when the predicate is reverted to the 203e31370 version (verify3/mut3.py d215_nosettle). Dropping only the delay, or only the second scan, does not make it fail. Two variants are still open. (1) verify3/test_probe_d215_lag.py: active_lag 7 and 10 are refused, but active_lag 15 and 30 are APPLIED at +16 s while the original TP is still open at the venue. The leg becomes REJECTED_ZERO_FILL, a second TP CID goes LIVE, and the cell has two open 10-LIT SELL TPs. With lag 30 the state stays NORMAL about 22 s before RISK_BLOCKED, and both orders remain open (verify3/test_probe_d215_detail30.py). The previous verifier's evidence explicitly listed lag 15. (2) The new WS clause does not work in production. `wake` files a fill signal under its trade id (engine.py:747-749), and the executor always passes exchange_trade_id, but the gate only checks `str(cid) in self.ws_pending` (engine.py:1451). In verify3/test_probe_d215_wsfill.py[False] the landed TP is fully filled, the WS hint {trade id -> TP cid} is pending, history lags 40 s and the filled order is correctly absent from the active list. resolve_unknown_submit is APPLIED at +12 s. The TP becomes REJECTED_ZERO_FILL and a second TP CID goes LIVE, although the 10 LIT were already sold (venue net 0). The hint then expires because REJECTED_ZERO_FILL counts as settled, so lag reads 0.0 before the trade is in history. The grid later turns FROZEN on the history conflict. A sibling probe, verify3/test_p2_resolve_ws_trade.py, independently targets the same gap.
open.residual_risk: An operator-audited 'not landed' can still create a new CID and a double or unbacked TP for a cell, and so exposure beyond the grid, in two cases: (a) the venue's active list lags more than about settlement_delay + 2 walks (~16 s with the defaults); (b) the order filled completely while history lags, even with a WS fill for that exact CID pending. Suggested fixes: check pending labels through `_ws_label_cid` values; do not treat an audit-made REJECTED_ZERO_FILL as settled when expiring labels; consider a cancel-by-CID before accepting absence.

open.evidence: ack_history_conflict now records audited payloads (accepted = committed fingerprint, noise = the other versions seen) in engine_meta within the command transaction (engine.py:1379-1390, 2203-2222). `_CursorView.audited_resolutions` (engine.py:299-309) serves them to the scanner, which skips audited noise (history.py:728-736). Re-ran scratchpad/verify/test_probe_ack_conflict.py: committed_payload_mismatch after the ack is NORMAL with history_complete True through 600 ticks. After a venue cancel the partially filled entry becomes TERMINAL (it used to stay TERMINAL_UNKNOWN), and STOP ends STOPPED_WITH_INVENTORY (it used to end STOP_UNCERTAIN). The persistent committed duplicate_key_payload_mismatch probe also completes. An orders-stream committed mismatch recovers too (verify3/test_probe_cr3_variants.py::test_c). review3::test_c3 fails when audited_resolutions returns [] and when `_audit_withheld_payloads` records nothing (verify3/mut3.py). Two variants are still open. (a) A persistent duplicate_key_payload_mismatch on a key that was never committed (both versions in the first walk): the ack is APPLIED with audited_payloads [] because engine.py:2212 skips keys with no committed payload. The grid stays RECONCILING with history_complete False after 120 ticks, and STOP ends STOP_UNCERTAIN (test_a). No audit action can lift this; the trace records it as intentional, pending R6. (b) engine.py:2219 replaces the key's audited entry instead of merging its noise. After ack1 (noise v1) and ack2 (noise v2), v1 reappearing conflicts again: RECONCILING, history incomplete, CELL_TP_BLOCKED (test_b). A venue alternating between two uncommitted versions therefore never converges.
open.residual_risk: This needs persistent venue misbehaviour. If a duplicate with differing payloads is never committed, or a key keeps flapping between two versions, the grid stays RECONCILING and entries stay blocked. Neither case has an audit path; STOP can only end STOP_UNCERTAIN, and the ack reports APPLIED although nothing was audited.

open.evidence: The original own-fill scenario is fixed and pinned. _audit_evidence_unsettled (engine.py:1194) refuses when position_seq < fills_commit_seq. Independently, _position_settled_for_audit (1216-1230) returns False when a fill was committed after the reads. The earlier probe verify/probe_d207.py at HEAD gives REJECTED with reasons ['position read predates the latest committed fill', 'position not yet stable ...']. With the whole ordering neutralised it gives APPLIED with new_effective_baseline 3. review3::test_d207_audit_refused_when_the_position_read_predates_a_committed_fill passes at HEAD. It fails under the line-1194-only removal (the audit is still rejected, but the 'predates' assert fails) and under full neutralisation (APPLIED, new_effective_baseline '-4'). However, fills_commit_seq advances only on own new_fills (1286-1287, 1759-1761), so the finding's broader case, a position read older than the last committed history batch, is still reachable with an unmatched trade. Probes verify3/test_probe_v4_d207.py and test_probe_v4_d207_after.py at HEAD: manual BUY 7, the position is stable, a poll reads 7, a manual BUY 2 follows, and the next tick's walk commits it as inbox row 4 (no poll). A BASELINE_AUDIT with observed 7 is then APPLIED with acknowledged_unmatched [2, 4] and new_effective_baseline 7 while the venue is 9. Line 1175 acknowledges every unmatched trade, including the one the read predates. Afterwards the engine is NORMAL with no entry blockers for about 32 s (B 7, P 7, venue 9). Only then does POSITION_UNRECONCILED fire, and a second audit is needed. That is the finding's consequence (another audit required, the rebase compared against a stale read), triggered by a manual trade instead of an own fill.
open.residual_risk: An audit can rebase on a read that predates a committed unmatched trade and mark that trade as acknowledged although B excludes it. The audit trail is misleading, and entries stay unblocked for up to position_gap_grace_s with an unaccounted manual position before POSITION_UNRECONCILED fires. Fix: refuse while any history row (not only own fills) was committed after the position read, or acknowledge only inbox rows committed before that read.

open.evidence: The verifier's no-WS residual is closed only by the new 'ahead' check (engine.py:1207-1211), and that check is neither pinned nor fail-closed. HEAD: the earlier probe verify/test_probe_d18b.py (partial fill 4, history_lag 30 s, ws=False) is REJECTED for all 20 attempts with 'active orders show executions history has not delivered'. review3::test_d218 passes. (1) Not pinned: test_d218 fails only when BOTH round-3 checks are removed (d218_both gives APPLIED, new_effective_baseline '11'). With only the ahead check removed (d218_ahead), test_d218 passes and so do all 231 engine tests and all 171 web/controller tests (logs: verify3/web_d218_ahead.log). The reason is that _position_settled_for_audit alone holds only until iteration 13, and the test loops 12 times. Probe verify3/test_probe_v4_d218.py under d218_ahead: APPLIED with baseline 11 at iteration 13 (default settle 5 s) or iteration 8 (settle 0), with history lag 30 s or 120 s. With the ahead check present, all six variants and the liveness case (applies with 7 after history arrives) pass. A full fill is covered separately: the leg goes TERMINAL_UNKNOWN, which counts as unresolved. (2) Fail-open at HEAD: when the active-orders read fails, _refresh_account sets active_rows=None (line 1524). Line 1207 uses (self.active_rows or []), so the ahead check sees nothing, and the audit never requires fresh active rows. Probe verify3/test_probe_v4_d218_active_down.py uses the finding's scenario with no WS, history lag 30 s, plus fx.fail_next('active_orders', 1000) or only 3 failures. Result at HEAD: iterations 4-12 are rejected only by 'position not yet stable', then iteration 13 is APPLIED with new_effective_baseline '11' (should be 7). After history delivers the fill: P 15, venue 11, EngineState.NORMAL, reasons []. This is exactly the double count in the finding.
open.residual_risk: A dropped WS event, history lag beyond settlement_delay_s and an active-orders read failure lasting about three polls (a transient outage) together still let the rebase absorb an own fill into B. The result is a wrong effective baseline in the durable audit trail, P != venue while NORMAL, then POSITION_UNRECONCILED and a second audit. The essential check can also be deleted without any committed test failing. Fix: refuse the audit when active rows are unknown or older than the position read, and extend test_d218 (or add a test) so it fails when only the ahead check is removed.

open.evidence: The reported scenario is fixed. executor.py:306-328: _track_start now re-sends a launcher START that turned CONFLICT (or has no row) with a new key and fresh revisions, and surfaces REJECTED as start_error. I re-ran the earlier probe verify/test_probe_launcher_start.py::test_probe_resume_start_lost_when_older_command_applies_first. The web PAUSE is APPLIED, START ...-0 is CONFLICT/stale_at_apply, the re-sent START ...-1 is APPLIED, and stop_requested_ms is None (the resume took effect). Before the fix the START was lost and start_error was None. CTL::test_c4_launcher_start_that_turns_conflict_is_resent_and_the_resume_applies passes. Mutation (only 'record is None' re-sends) makes it fail (no APPLIED start with resume_stop_ms). However, the fix introduced a new variant, reproduced by verify3/v5/test_v5_cr4_variant.py::test_v5_cr4_variant_grid[False-ACCEPT-1] and [False-ACCEPT-2]. Setup: the previous process was killed mid-drain, so the durable stop S1 has stop_outcome None (STOPPING). A web PAUSE is queued while Hummingbot is down. The operator configures the resume phrase for S1 and runs Hummingbot `stop` before the first tick. Sequence: tick 1 applies the PAUSE, and START-0 and STOP-1 both turn CONFLICT. _track_stop re-sends STOP-2, then _track_start re-sends START-1. STOP-2 is APPLIED but keeps S1, because a STOP during STOPPING creates no new stop (engine.py:1022-1028), and _stop_command_sent becomes True. START-1 turns CONFLICT and START-2 is APPLIED with resume_stop_ms==S1, which clears stop_requested_ms. End state: stop None, engine PAUSED (it would be NORMAL without the PAUSE), close_type None. The executor never closes, the drain times out as STOP_NOT_APPLIED, and the next launch resumes trading without the resume phrase. Cause: _track_start keeps re-sending after _stop_requested is set, and nothing makes an APPLIED Hummingbot STOP invalidate an older resume that names the same STOPPING stop. Without the CR-4 fix (mutation) this variant does not occur.
open.residual_risk: The window is narrow. It needs all of: a crash or forced exit during a previous drain (outcome None), a command queued while Hummingbot was down (or other CONFLICT churn), a resume phrase for that stop, and a Hummingbot stop issued before the tick in which the START conflicts (about 1 s). The operator's stop is then undone. It is logged as STOP_NOT_APPLIED, but the next start trades. Suggested fix: do not re-send START once _stop_requested (or drop the pending START intent in early_stop), and/or have the engine reject a launcher resume whose START row was created before a later APPLIED STOP.

New probes in verify3/test_v3_b09.py, 6 passed: (a) after a restart, both NOT_SENT and DEFINITIVE_REJECT_ZERO_FILL on the DISPATCHED row keep SUBMIT_UNKNOWN and the reservation, and a new ENTRY revision is refused with 'cycle already has entry leg ... in SUBMIT_UNKNOWN'; (b) restart, then resend_same_cid, then NOT_SENT also stays UNKNOWN; (c) set_leg_state or the leg_state refinement to REJECTED_UNSENT, REJECTED_ZERO_FILL or TERMINAL is refused without venue evidence; (d) control: a pre-send NOT_SENT in the same process still releases. The engine records NOT_SENT only for PENDING rows (engine.py:1964-1976, 2675-2683, 2701-2705). Other exceptions become UNKNOWN (engine.py:2535-2549). Unmodified: the b09 and review4_release tests pass (5 passed).
results.residual_risk: None found. The rule is conservative: reopening the store inside the same process also counts as 'another process', so such a row stays UNKNOWN until history evidence or an audited reconciliation.

results.evidence: The engine now rewrites the health sidecar at least every health_heartbeat_s=10 s even when healthy (engine.py:872-885, data_types.py:49). It writes it in tick()'s finally block (engine.py:771-778). The web health_view (views.py:250-282) treats a health_file sidecar whose 'at' is older than stale_after_s as known=False. When the snapshot is stale it shows the banner 'Снимок устарел, а состояние хранилища неизвестно (файл здоровья движка устарел N с)', and app.js:431-439 renders health.banner. I re-ran the headline scenario with a real Harness (verify3/probe_e03_v3.py): a read-only data directory plus simulate_disk_full, so every sidecar write fails and the file keeps the old healthy content. The result, with the default stale_after=15: NORMAL/known=True until t+15 s, then STALE, health_known=False and the unknown-storage banner at every later sample up to t+70 s. It also works with stale_after=60 (flips at 60 s) and with stale_after=5 (smaller than the heartbeat). The earlier verifier result (known=True, banner=None next to a stale snapshot) no longer occurs. Revert check: mutating the outdated test in health_view makes test_ngweb_round3.py::test_e03_outdated_healthy_sidecar_is_unknown_next_to_stale fail. Removing the heartbeat condition in _write_health makes test_ng_engine_review3.py::test_e03_health_sidecar_heartbeat_even_when_healthy fail. Both pass unmodified.
results.residual_risk: Low, and inherent to attach mode on an unwritable filesystem. The UI says the storage state is unknown and the snapshot is stale, but it cannot name the actual error (for example SQLITE_FULL), which the CLI status prints as LOCAL ERROR. For the first stale_after_s seconds after the failure the UI still shows the last committed state (for example NORMAL) with a growing age. The web does not check the filesystem itself (statvfs or writability) to say 'disk full'.

results.evidence: Engine: START stores meta.start_config_fingerprint = full_fingerprint, a sha256 of every GridConfig field except enabled (engine.py:424-426, 1000-1004). Before bootstrap, _cmd_confirm_baseline refuses START_CONFIG_CHANGED on a mismatch and resets started=False (engine.py:1085-1092). meta is persisted in the same transaction even for REJECTED (engine.py:936-940). A legacy START without a fingerprint compares as None, so it also fails closed. Web: the START payload gets material_id (config + rules without revisions, preview.py:127-133), added at enqueue (commands.py:324). confirm_baseline returns 409 start_material_changed when the latest APPLIED START's material_id differs from the current engine_config/runtime_rules preview (commands.py:215-227, 298-301). Re-ran the verifier probe verify/probe_e_restart_cfg.py (START for Q=10, restart with Q=20 and caps 2000 before bootstrap, then CONFIRM_BASELINE B=0). It is now REJECTED with START_CONFIG_CHANGED and bootstrapped=False (before the fix it was APPLIED and bootstrapped the Q=20 grid). Revert check: removing the engine check fails test_ng_engine_review3.py::test_e09_confirm_baseline_refuses_a_config_changed_after_start, and stubbing _start_material_blocker fails test_ngweb_round3.py::test_e09_confirm_baseline_refused_when_material_changed_since_start. Both pass unmodified. The original literal scenario (a separate web YAML) was already fixed: identity and preview come from the snapshot's engine_config.
results.residual_risk: Low, a narrow race outside the reported window, found with verify3/probe_e09_race.py. A web START is enqueued against config A's snapshot, and the engine restarts with config B before claiming it. A pre-bootstrap restart does not bump config or engine revisions, so the START is APPLIED and the engine records B's fingerprint as the one acknowledged; material_id A is stored but only as information. The web confirm_baseline still blocks this, because material A differs from B. A CONFIRM_BASELINE from outside the web (launcher operator_confirmed_baseline) is accepted and bootstrapped the Q=20 grid in the probe. The launcher's confirmation phrase covers only grid_id and B, not Q or caps.

results.evidence: Port: every read (trading_rules, position, active_orders, inactive_orders_page, trades_page) goes through _sanitized (lighter_port.py:256-282), which re-raises a text-free LighterPortRequestError('<op> failed: <Type>') outside the handler, so there is no __cause__ or __context__. submit and cancel already returned only the type name (lighter_port.py:441-455; connector submit/cancel details are type-only). Engine: redact() (engine.py:172-186) cuts URL query strings, auth/token/signature/Authorization values and long hex. It is applied in _error (engine.py:909), in persistence errors, incomplete reasons and transport details (_call, engine.py:2544-2548). Web: redact_tree/redact_free_text runs at server._json (server.py:96-98) and also covers quoted-key forms. Re-running the original probe verify/test_scratch_auth_leak.py: both leak-asserting tests now FAIL (the port raises 'active_orders failed: ContentTypeError', and the committed snapshot no longer contains the token), so the reported leak is gone. An extended engine probe (verify3/test_v3_cr1.py) raised URL-form and Authorization-header-form token text from all five endpoints. It found no token in the snapshot, errors, format_status, caplog, health or the raw DB/WAL bytes; history pages show only 'page_fetch_error:<stream>:RuntimeError'. Revert check: a pass-through _sanitized fails test_c1_lighter_port_wraps_non_history_errors_with_type_only_detail, and an identity engine.redact fails test_c1_auth_token_never_reaches_snapshot_errors_status_logs_or_the_ledger. Unmodified, the engine C1 tests, the WS-C port tests (2 passed, 5 subtests) and the web C1 tests (2 passed) all pass.
results.residual_risk: Low, defence in depth only. The engine redact regex misses quoted-key forms ({'auth': 'X'}, {"auth": "X"}) and short bare tokens: my engine-level probe that bypassed the real port leaked those into the snapshot, errors, CLI status and the SQLite file. The web layer redacts the quoted forms. The production LighterExchangePort never passes exception text through, so this cannot happen today; it would matter only if a future port or adapter forwarded raw exception text. A real Lighter token's hex signature is redacted by the long-hex rule.

results.evidence: The original own-fill scenario is fixed and pinned. _audit_evidence_unsettled (engine.py:1194) refuses when position_seq < fills_commit_seq. It fails under the line-1194-only removal (the audit is still rejected, but the 'predates' assert fails) and under full neutralisation (APPLIED, new_effective_baseline '-4'). However, fills_commit_seq advances only on own new_fills (1286-1287, 1759-1761), so the finding's broader case, a position read older than the last committed history batch, is still reachable with an unmatched trade. Probes verify3/test_probe_v4_d207.py and test_probe_v4_d207_after.py at HEAD: manual BUY 7, the position is stable, a poll reads 7, a manual BUY 2 follows, and the next tick's walk commits it as inbox row 4 (no poll). A BASELINE_AUDIT with observed 7 is then APPLIED with acknowledged_unmatched [2, 4] and new_effective_baseline 7 while the venue is 9. Line 1175 acknowledges every unmatched trade, including the one the read predates. Afterwards the engine is NORMAL with no entry blockers for about 32 s (B 7, P 7, venue 9). Only then does POSITION_UNRECONCILED fire, and a second audit is needed. That is the finding's consequence (another audit required, the rebase compared against a stale read), triggered by a manual trade instead of an own fill.
results.residual_risk: An audit can rebase on a read that predates a committed unmatched trade and mark that trade as acknowledged although B excludes it. The audit trail is misleading, and entries stay unblocked for up to position_gap_grace_s with an unaccounted manual position before POSITION_UNRECONCILED fires. Fix: refuse while any history row (not only own fills) was committed after the position read, or acknowledge only inbox rows committed before that read.

results.evidence: The reported scenario is fixed. executor.py:306-328: _track_start now re-sends a launcher START that turned CONFLICT (or has no row) with a new key and fresh revisions, and surfaces REJECTED as start_error. I re-ran the earlier probe verify/test_probe_launcher_start.py::test_probe_resume_start_lost_when_older_command_applies_first. The web PAUSE is APPLIED, START ...-0 is CONFLICT/stale_at_apply, the re-sent START ...-1 is APPLIED, and stop_requested_ms is None (the resume took effect). Before the fix the START was lost and start_error was None. CTL::test_c4_launcher_start_that_turns_conflict_is_resent_and_the_resume_applies passes. Mutation (only 'record is None' re-sends) makes it fail (no APPLIED start with resume_stop_ms). However, the fix introduced a new variant, reproduced by verify3/v5/test_v5_cr4_variant.py::test_v5_cr4_variant_grid[False-ACCEPT-1] and [False-ACCEPT-2]. Setup: the previous process was killed mid-drain, so the durable stop S1 has stop_outcome None (STOPPING). A web PAUSE is queued while Hummingbot is down. The operator configures the resume phrase for S1 and runs Hummingbot `stop` before the first tick. Sequence: tick 1 applies the PAUSE, and START-0 and STOP-1 both turn CONFLICT. _track_stop re-sends STOP-2, then _track_start re-sends START-1. STOP-2 is APPLIED but keeps S1, because a STOP during STOPPING creates no new stop (engine.py:1022-1028), and _stop_command_sent becomes True. START-1 turns CONFLICT and START-2 is APPLIED with resume_stop_ms==S1, which clears stop_requested_ms. End state: stop None, engine PAUSED (it would be NORMAL without the PAUSE), close_type None. The executor never closes, the drain times out as STOP_NOT_APPLIED, and the next launch resumes trading without the resume phrase. Cause: _track_start keeps re-sending after _stop_requested is set, and nothing makes an APPLIED Hummingbot STOP invalidate an older resume that names the same STOPPING stop. Without the CR-4 fix (mutation) this variant does not occur.
results.residual_risk: The window is narrow. It needs all of: a crash or forced exit during a previous drain (outcome None), a command queued while Hummingbot was down (or other CONFLICT churn), a resume phrase for that stop, and a Hummingbot stop issued before the tick in which the START conflicts (about 1 s). The operator's stop is then undone. It is logged as STOP_NOT_APPLIED, but the next start trades. Suggested fix: do not re-send START once _stop_requested (or drop the pending START intent in early_stop), and/or have the engine reject a launcher resume whose START row was created before a later APPLIED STOP.

critic.title: resolve_unknown_submit WS gate only checks a CID label, but WS fill signals are stored under their trade id, so a filled order can be recorded as 'never landed' and the grid places a second exit order
critic.requirement: D2-15 (trace ws-d-engine.md line 298): resolve_unknown_submit needs 'no pending WS signal for that CID'. AC-40 / NG-HIST-001: quantity is never guessed and a zero-fill resolution needs proof of absence.
critic.failure_scenario: A TP submit times out but lands (SUBMIT_UNKNOWN) and fills fully right away. The WS OrderFilledEvent arrives. The executor passes it on with exchange_trade_id, so engine.wake stores it as ws_pending[<trade_id>], with _ws_label_cid[<trade_id>] = cid. Venue history lags longer than settlement_delay_s. The order is not in active orders because it is filled. The operator (or a retry) sends resolve_unknown_submit, and _absence_not_proven only tests `str(cid) in self.ws_pending`, which is false. The leg is recorded as REJECTED_ZERO_FILL ('not_landed'), the cell's reservation is released, and a new SELL TP for the same 10 base goes LIVE while the venue position is already flat. If that TP fills, the account is short 10 until the delayed history shows up as a late fill. In production a WS trade event always carries exchange_trade_id, so the CID-label check practically never fires. The trade-id label also stops counting as lag once the leg is final (_own_live_label), so the signal disappears.

critic.title: Executor keeps re-sending the launcher resume START after Hummingbot asked it to stop, and this undoes an applied STOP
critic.requirement: NG-OPS-003 / AC-35/36: an applied STOP is durable and is never resumed automatically; the Hummingbot stop is the operator's own intent and must drain to a stopped engine.
critic.failure_scenario: Setup: the previous Hummingbot run was killed while STOPPING (stop_requested_ms=S, stop_outcome=None). The operator relaunches with the resume phrase naming S, and a web command was queued while Hummingbot was down (the c4 race), or the START insert hit SQLITE_BUSY. The operator then types `stop` right after launch. Tick 1: the web PAUSE applies, launcher START K0 goes CONFLICT, and the executor STOP S1 goes CONFLICT. _track_stop re-sends S2, then _track_start re-sends K1. Tick 2: S2 is APPLIED. Because stop_outcome is None, the STOP handler keeps stop_requested_ms=S, and K1 goes CONFLICT. _track_start does not check _stop_requested and sends K2. Tick 3: K2 carries resume_stop_ms == S, which still matches, so it is APPLIED. The stop is cleared and the executor never closes (is_stopped is false). The operator's applied Hummingbot STOP is silently reverted and the grid keeps its live orders and trading.

critic.title: ack_history_conflict silently audits away contradictions that appeared after the operator's reviewed snapshot (the ack is not bound to what was seen)
critic.requirement: Spec §history: one key with a different payload means a history conflict and a pause. AC-40: a history conflict stops exposure and quantity is never guessed. C3 claim: 'a version never seen at the audit stays a conflict'. Web/engine commands carry expected revisions so they do not apply to a state the operator did not see.
critic.failure_scenario: The engine is FROZEN on trade conflict X, and the operator reviews it at revision (1,5). Afterwards the venue starts serving a contradicting payload for a different committed row, for example the filled order's filled_base_amount goes from 10 to 7. The engine is already FROZEN and manual_reconcile_required is already set, so engine_revision does not change, manual_reconcile_reason still names only X, and no store conflict is opened. The operator's ack_history_conflict at (1,5) is therefore not stale and applies. _audit_withheld_payloads records every withheld version from the latest walk as 'noise', including the unseen filled=7 order row, then clears the freeze. Later walks skip it, history becomes complete and the engine returns to NORMAL. The venue's contradicting quantity is permanently hidden, and the operator never saw it.

critic.title: START that acknowledges a changed config is answered 'already_started' without re-binding start_config_fingerprint, so CONFIRM_BASELINE is refused (launcher path stuck until another restart)
critic.requirement: E-09 / NG-UI-002: baseline confirmation is bound to the config the applied START acknowledged; a new START for the current preview must make the baseline confirmable.
critic.failure_scenario: A START is applied under config C1. The engine restarts with a changed config C2 before bootstrap. This also covers a pre-round-3 ledger with START applied but not bootstrapped, where start_config_fingerprint is None. The launcher sends its START on every start (a web operator would do the same), and the engine returns APPLIED {'already_started': True} at line 995 without setting start_config_fingerprint. The next CONFIRM_BASELINE is REJECTED START_CONFIG_CHANGED, telling the operator to send a new START, which they just did. In the executor, START_CONFIG_CHANGED is not in _TRANSIENT_BASELINE_ERRORS and the START key was already cleared as APPLIED, so _baseline_refused latches. The grid stays unbootstrapped until Hummingbot is restarted again.
